structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery` are the public type and signatures: `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct TextQuery` with fields `scope: SourceScope`, `pattern: String`, `context_lines: usize` and `limit: Option<usize>`. They also include the builder-style `new(String)`, `scope(self, SourceScope)`, `context_lines(self, usize)` and `limit(self, usize)`, each returning `Self`. The default values are the only other obligation: all visible files, zero context lines and no limit.

Each obligation maps to a root in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs`:
- `struct[TextQuery]` declares `#[non_exhaustive]` and exactly the four required public fields with the required types.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[new]` takes `pattern: String` and returns `Self`. It sets `scope` to `SourceScope::all()`, `context_lines` to 0 and `limit` to `None`. `SourceScope::all()` is documented as selecting all visible project files and delegates to `Self::default()`. I did not read `SourceScope`'s `Default` implementation.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[scope]` is `fn(mut self, SourceScope) -> Self` and overrides `scope`.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[context_lines]` is `fn(mut self, usize) -> Self` and overrides `context_lines`.
- `impl[TextQuery]/fn[limit]` is `fn(mut self, usize) -> Self` and sets `limit = Some(limit)`.

All five roots carry `{impl}` markers. The remaining clauses are observable behavior, so they create no structural obligation. These clauses cover `pattern` being a regular expression, `context_lines` returning that many surrounding lines, and `limit` bounding matches across the scope. The behavioral criterion covers them.

behavioral: The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery`.

- **Defaults from `new`:**
  - The test asserts `query.limit == None` and `query.context_lines == 0`.
  - The default scope is all visible files. `TextQuery::new("^hit[0-9]$")` returns 3 matches across `one.txt` and `two.txt`, so the default covers more than one file.
  - Zero context returns just the matching line. Every excerpt in the default result starts with `hit` and has length 4.
- **`pattern` is a regex:** `^hit[0-9]$` and `^hit$` only match as regular expressions. The anchors and character class are what select the right lines.
- **`scope` override:** `.scope(SourceScope::under("one.txt"))` limits results to `one.txt`. The test checks the exact path, line and excerpt tuples.
- **`context_lines` override:**
  - Context 1 and context 2 are each checked against exact excerpts on the same hit.
  - The context is applied on both sides of the hit.
  - Excerpts are clipped at the start of a file (`hit1\nmiddle`) and at the end (`middle\nhit2`).
- **`limit` override:**
  - `limit(2)` over 3 matches in two files returns 2 matches and `complete == false`. This shows the limit applies across the scope rather than per file.
  - `limit(2)` where exactly 2 matches exist returns `complete == true`.
  - `limit(1)` returns 1 match and `complete == false`.
  - The default `None` limit returns all 3 matches with `complete == true`.
- **Struct and method signatures:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against rustdoc. The first test also uses the builder methods and reads the `limit` and `context_lines` fields, and its assertions on `pattern` access are only partly relevant.

I found no untested behavioral obligation. The requirement does not specify behavior for an invalid regex or `limit(0)`, so those are not gaps.

text: `TextQuery::new(pattern)` searches all visible files, with zero context lines and
no match limit. `scope`, `context_lines`, and `limit` override those defaults.

`pattern` is a regular expression. `context_lines` requests that many lines on either side of each matching line. Zero returns just the matching line. `limit` bounds matches across the scope. `None` requests all matches.
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn context_lines(self, context_lines: usize) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
